in_hebrew.name: עגירון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עגרון (עָגִירוֹן) - צבאי, גדוד, איש צבא. בעברית עתיקה, המילה עגירון מיוחסת לעגר, כלומר 'להכין' או 'להכניס'. כיום, השם עגירון נפוץ כשם משפחה, ובו נגזרה הצורה עגירון.

in_greek.name: Γαρίσων
in_greek.long_meaning: Γαρίσων (Γαρίσων) - στρατηγός, διοικητής, αξιωματικός. Η λέξη Γαρίσων προέρχεται από τα αρχαία ελληνικά και αναφέρεται σε ένα αξιωματικό ή διοικητή. Στη Βίβλο, ο Γαρίσων είναι ένα επώνυμο που αναφέρεται σε έναν στρατηγό από την Ταρσό (Κολόσσαι 4:11-12).

in_latin.name: Garrison
in_latin.long_meaning: Garrison - miles, armiger, miles Romanus. Latinus origo nominis a milite, armiger, miles Romanus. Nomen militare originem habet ab armigero, qui miles erat Romani exercitus.

in_english.name: Garrison
in_english.meaning: a military officer, a fortification, or a stronghold
in_english.long_meaning: Garrison - a military officer, a fortification, or a stronghold. The name Garrison has its origins in the Old French word 'garrison', which means a group of soldiers stationed in a fortified place. In the Christian tradition, the name Garrison is associated with strength, courage, and protection. It is also linked to the biblical figure of Garrison, a Roman officer who was converted to Christianity (Acts 6:5).

seo.description_paragraph: The Old English name Garrison is derived from the words 'gars' (spear) and 'dun' (hill), which metaphorically represent a person of great strength, courage, and determination. Garrison was commonly used as a name for those living in fortified areas, such as castle towns or strongholds. In Christianity, the name is associated with the idea of a spiritual fortress, offering protection and security from the challenges of life. Today, Garrison is a popular name for boys, reflecting its enduring appeal and timeless significance.
